summary: Build practical skills to design exposure-monitoring plans, interpret hygiene measurements, and prioritize workplace risk controls. Ideal for HSSE managers.
lede: Occupational hygiene training helps safety professionals assess workplace hazards and plan exposure monitoring. It is for HSSE managers, occupational health staff, safety officers and site managers responsible for workplace health risks. Learners develop exposure-monitoring plans, group workers with similar exposures, interpret exposure and noise measurements, assess heat data, and prioritize controls using the Hierarchy of Controls.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for workplace health, safety, and environmental risk management in industrial, construction, and energy sectors.
modules: Foundations of Occupational Hygiene and Exposure Science
Airborne Hazards: Dust, Particulates, and Silica
Chemical Hazards: Vapours, Gases, and VOCs
Physical Hazards: Noise Dosimetry and Mapping
Thermal Hazards: Heat Stress and WBGT
prerequisites: Participants should have a foundational understanding of general workplace health and safety principles. Familiarity with basic mathematical calculations (averages, percentages) is required for interpreting exposure data. No prior qualification as an industrial hygienist is necessary.
